01 / A shared visual language

Start with a consistent foundation.

Buttons, fields, cards and layouts belong together. Five themes, two densities and semantic color roles carry the same visual language into every module.

A complete everyday toolkit

Forms, tables, navigation, status messages and notifications share the active theme. Ordinary Dear ImGui widgets continue to work alongside CyUI.

Made for dense workspaces

Choose compact or comfortable density. Semantic sizing and per-context DPI/font configuration let the host adapt the interface to its displays.

English first. French included.

Switch language while retaining widget identities. Extend the shared catalogue with your application’s translations and additional languages.

02 / Editor tools

Give every asset a place.

Build content browsers with real folder navigation, grid or list views, thumbnails and selection metadata. Connect the same resources to clear, typed details panels.

  • Hierarchical navigation and drag/drop
  • Editable, grouped properties
  • Optional search in menus and panels
Build an editor panel ↗

Details without duplication.

Strings, choices, toggles and numeric fields, with draft edits and validation. Your application owns the object, the preview and its Undo history.

Explore the guide ↗

Find the control. Keep your focus.

Search across nested actions or properties. Match English and translated captions, ignore Latin accents, and use Ctrl/Cmd+F or Escape in the focused view.

Explore the guide ↗

Actions at your fingertips.

A searchable command palette returns stable action IDs. The host decides which commands are enabled and performs the requested operation.

Read what your tools report.

Display bounded logs and diagnostic lists with severity, filtering and navigation. The example messages shown here are synthetic.

03 / Canvas / nodes / curves

Think in connections.

Compose visual editors from connected cards and pins. Navigation, selection, movement and layout share one canvas foundation; your application owns graph compatibility and execution.

The demo host prepares these synthetic textures. CyUI displays them inside the nodes; it does not execute image-processing or shader algorithms.

Visual logic, clearly laid out.

Typed-looking pins, curved links and navigable cards give your graph a readable shape. Pin types, validation and evaluation are supplied by the host.

Explore the guide ↗

Make the movement editable.

Edit keyframes, handles and selection with snapping and explicit edit transactions. Connect the proposals to your application’s automation and Undo system.

Explore the guide ↗

04 / Audio & data

Make your signals readable.

Waveforms, spectra, oscilloscopes and stereo scopes sit alongside familiar knobs, faders and meters. Use the same visual system for creative audio tools and technical analysis.

AudioViews draws data prepared by your application. Audio decoding, FFTs and signal processing remain in your engine.

Explore data views ↗

A shared audio analysis workspace.

Inspect time and frequency with a spectrogram, compare LUFS histories, show true peaks and stereo correlation, edit EQ handles over gain/phase curves, and display dynamics with gain reduction. Available in the current sources and Audio analysis gallery tab.

Explore spectral detail and stereo space.

Use filled curves and frequency bands with a dB floor. Follow scrolling spectrograms in either orientation, with intensity or frequency grading and color legends. Add a spatial stereo cloud or a persistent vectorscope with adjustable fading and glow.

From a series to an overview.

Linear and logarithmic axes, lines, points, steps, bars, histograms and heatmaps. Feed bounded or reduced datasets from your application.

Explore the guide ↗

Give time a structure.

Move and trim clips, select time ranges and display markers. Time units, transport, media decoding and project state belong to the host.

Explore the guide ↗

05 / Code / editing / diff

Read, edit, compare.

Use a shared syntax catalogue across source views, the native editor and comparisons. Add annotations or register your own language rules and lexer callbacks.

  • Native C++ editing with Undo/Redo
  • Shared language profiles and shader syntax
  • Unified and side-by-side comparisons
Code integration guide ↗

Keep both sides in view.

Aligned rows, highlighted changes and navigation between hunks make revisions easier to read. CyUI displays prepared text comparisons; Git, repository access and merge operations stay in the application.

06 / Images / viewports / documents

The rest of the workspace belongs here, too.

Bring image tools, rendered surfaces and readable documents into the same interface. These modules handle presentation and interaction; the host supplies textures, content and services.

Images & gradients

Navigate textures, adjust a crop and edit gradient stops. Decoding and image processing stay in your application.

Explore the guide ↗

Host-rendered viewports

An orbit-camera model and transform overlays surround a host-rendered surface. The preview texture is synthetic; CyUI is not a 3D engine.

Documents & conversations

Render a Markdown subset, code blocks, tables and transcripts. Conversation models, networking and AI providers belong to the host.

08 / One foundation, several hosts

Your application sets the boundaries.

Keep project models, file access, processing and services in the host. CyUI gives them a consistent presentation, with explicit state and edit proposals.

Native

C++

Compile against your host’s existing ImGui target. Core needs C++17; the native CodeEditor and tested CEF adapter use C++20.

Integration guide ↗
Python

imgui-bundle

Import optional families explicitly. Models are available without a renderer; Python’s editor has multiline editing and a syntax preview.

Integration guide ↗
Web / CEF

HTML + TypeScript

Embed a browser surface through a backend or the optional off-screen CEF adapter. Compile TypeScript in your web app and exchange versioned messages.

Integration guide ↗
Unreal Editor

An optional connector

Embed CyUI in Slate panels inside another plugin. Select the modules you need and share a provider or package a uniquely named copy. Editor-only.

Integration guide ↗

Choose dependencies deliberately.

This example links Nodes and Inspector through your existing ImGui target. Their required CyUI dependencies follow automatically.

CMake ≥ 3.16 · Dear ImGui ≥ 1.92. Integration uses add_subdirectory or FetchContent; there is no installed find_package(CyUI) package.

CMakeLists.txt
set(CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET app_imgui)
set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF)
set(CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF)
set(CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF)
set(CYUI_MODULES "Nodes;Inspector")
add_subdirectory(external/CyUI)

target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE
    CyUI::Nodes CyUI::Inspector)

Before you start

A few useful answers.

Scope, platforms and the parts your application keeps.

Is CyUI an application or a library?

CyUI is a themed widget and interface-module library built on Dear ImGui. The downloadable application is its interactive gallery. It does not replace your application’s engine, project model or rendering backend.

Is this an alpha or beta?

The repository identifies the current library and demo as version 1.2.0 and is under active development. It does not declare an alpha or beta designation. Test the modules and adapters against your host and target platforms before distribution.

Can I use it in commercial software?

CyUI’s own code and adapters use the MIT license. Keep its copyright and permission notice, together with the licenses of the dependencies you distribute. CEF and Unreal Engine retain their separate terms.

Do I have to use all the modules?

No. Begin with Core and explicitly select additional targets. Their dependency closure is linked automatically. WebCEF, ImGuizmo and the Unreal Editor connector are optional integrations with separately supplied dependencies.

Does the documentation work offline?

Yes. The complete English/French CyDoc reader is included with this site and current source builds. Keep the Documentation folder together and open Documentation.html directly from disk. External references, GitHub and downloads need a connection.
